clue.text: Thanks Mr Hackman expressly for the stew

indicators.note: to express something is to put it into speech, so the actor's first name is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: ta is informal British for thank you
the actor Gene Hackman's first name, spelt as it is pronounced

explanation.surface: A grateful nod to the actor Gene Hackman for cooking the stew.
explanation.walkthrough: TAJINE is a variant spelling of tagine; its second syllable is said exactly like the name Gene.
explanation.definitionFit: A tajine is a slow-cooked North African stew named after the conical earthenware pot it is made in.

clue.text: Rex scarpered, taking a month to make the  crossing

blocks.note: read as T. Rex, the dinosaur, leaving its T
scarpered is British slang for ran away
the short form of September

explanation.surface: Someone called Rex ran off and spent a month getting across.
explanation.walkthrough: T + RAN + SEPT: the clue seems to rely on 'Rex' calling up T. Rex, the band or the dinosaur, to supply the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The transept is the arm of a cross-shaped church that crosses the nave, and the space where they meet is called the crossing.

clue.text: A cooler turkey, perhaps, is one in the coop?

blocks.note: the cooler is slang for prison
a turkey is one example of a bird

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a chilled turkey belongs in the chicken coop.
explanation.walkthrough: Coop is slang for prison, which is why the definition carries a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A jailbird is a prisoner or habitual criminal, and coop is a slang word for a prison cell.

clue.text: Grannie certainly bore one of the brood

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the words carry the answer within their letters

blocks.note: sits across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A grandmother proudly recalls giving birth to one of her many children.
explanation.definitionFit: Brood is used loosely for a whole family, and a brother's or sister's daughter is one member of it.

clue.text: Cancel return of Basque militants with former Soviet president's majority

indicators.note: returning sends everything back the way it came, so the whole string is read from right to left
the majority is the larger part, so the surname loses its tail

blocks.note: ETA was the Basque separatist group
the first five letters of Gorbachev, most of the name

explanation.surface: A political headline about scrapping something once Basque separatists and Gorbachev get involved.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrogate a law or treaty is formally to repeal or annul it, which is to cancel it.

clue.text: Maybe Pugh's an expert at the game

blocks.note: Pugh sounds like Pew, the blind beggar in Treasure Island, so 'maybe' he is a blind man
a buff is an enthusiast who knows a lot

explanation.surface: A boast that someone called Pugh is a whizz at some game.
explanation.walkthrough: Blind Pew is the sinister blind pirate in Stevenson's Treasure Island; Pugh is a sound-alike spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Blind man's buff is a children's party game in which a blindfolded player tries to catch the others.

clue.text: The boat from Oxford University set off

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
to set off a reaction is to trigger it

explanation.surface: The Oxford rowing crew's boat pushes off from the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrigger is a narrow canoe or racing boat with a float or rowlock bracket projecting from its side.

clue.text: Stood and endured

blocks.note: first meaning: put up with, as in could not stand or abide it
second meaning: lasted or remained

explanation.walkthrough: Stood looks like a physical position, but it means tolerated.
explanation.definitionFit: Abide covers both tolerating something unpleasant and continuing to exist, and this is a past-tense form of it.

clue.text: You once took Mona back... no hassle?

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one word wraps around the other
going back means the combined string is read from its last letter to its first

blocks.note: ye is the old form of you
the Mona Lisa, Leonardo's portrait

explanation.surface: An old flame recalls how effortlessly they once took Mona home.
explanation.walkthrough: YE holds LISA to make YLISAE, which reads EASILY backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something easily means doing it without trouble or effort, which is with no hassle at all.

clue.text: One (new) knight's stand?

blocks.note: first meaning: the word that belongs to a newly dubbed knight, told to get up by the monarch
second meaning: get up, rise to one's feet

explanation.walkthrough: At a dubbing the sovereign says 'Arise, Sir...', so this is the new knight's word; it is also a plain verb for standing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise is to get up from sitting or kneeling, and it is the formal command that ends the knighting ceremony.

clue.text: Makes good preserves

blocks.note: first meaning: keeps in repair, as with a building
second meaning: keeps something going or in existence

explanation.walkthrough: Preserves looks like a noun for jam, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both repairing and upkeep of property and keeping a state of affairs unchanged.

clue.text: Oklahoma supports game

blocks.note: Oklahoma! is a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show, an example of the genre
chairs are things that support a sitter

explanation.surface: The state of Oklahoma backs some sporting contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical chairs is a party game where players circle seats while music plays and scramble to sit when it stops.

clue.text: Developing buds seem to have resistance under water

indicators.note: something developing is changing its form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that sprouting buds seem tough when kept underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Submersed is a botanical term for plants growing entirely beneath the surface of water.

clue.text: One to cope with a  husband...

definitions.note: the gap in the title of Wilde's play An Ideal Husband

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
to deal with something is to cope with it

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to put up with a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in-the-blank: Oscar Wilde's comedy An Ideal Husband. The ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde's play title supplies the missing adjective, describing a perfect spouse.

clue.text: ... rapt?

blocks.note: surface reading: a continuation of the previous clue, someone enthralled by an ideal husband
setter's reading: this word is what you get when the letters of a four-letter word for a portion are swapped around

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the instruction that produces the clue. Exchange the letters of PART and you get RAPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Part exchange is the trade-in of an old item as partial payment for a new one, here read literally as swapping a word's letters.

clue.text: Pushed out, you said?

definitions.note: said, as in put into words

blocks.note: first meaning: squeezed out, as juice or milk
second meaning: put into words

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from one verb: pressing out liquid, and putting a thought into words.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both squeezing something out under pressure and stating a feeling or idea in words.

clue.text: Lent is brought forward

blocks.note: first meaning: paid out money ahead of time as a loan
second meaning: moved on or moved earlier

explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes Lent look like the Christian season before Easter, but it is the past tense of lend.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid before it is due is advanced to the borrower, and a date or army moved forward has advanced.

clue.text: A scrap of a form?

blocks.note: surface reading: a torn fragment of paperwork
setter's reading: a fight, with a form meaning a school year group and hence a social stratum

explanation.walkthrough: Scrap means a fight, and form is a school class; the answer is conflict between social classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Class war is the political struggle between social ranks such as workers and owners, a fight between kinds of class.

clue.text: Pudding on plate slurped all over the place

indicators.note: something spread all over the place is in total disorder, so these letters are scattered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A messy diner has slopped dessert across the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple strudel is a Central European dessert of spiced apple rolled in thin layered pastry; pudding is British for dessert.

clue.text: Put on your warm coat and hold your tongue!

blocks.note: first meaning: dress warmly
second meaning: British slang for be quiet

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves sound like a parent's orders; the phrase means bundle up and also shut up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both bundling up against the cold and, as a rude command, telling someone to stop talking.

clue.text: New crime wave presents a poser

indicators.note: a wave sets things moving and tumbling, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh spate of offending creates a puzzle for the police.
explanation.walkthrough: A poser here is an affected show-off, not a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: One who minces walks or talks with exaggerated daintiness, so the word fits someone striking an affected pose.

clue.text: Build beams noisily

indicators.note: done noisily means the word is heard, so its pronunciation counts rather than spelling

blocks.note: beams of light are rays

explanation.surface: Construction girders are put up with a lot of din.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a building or wall is to erect or build it.

clue.text: No middle-aged spread for this old-timer!

definitions.text: No middle-aged spread for this old-timer!

blocks.clueFragment: No middle-aged spread for this old-timer!
blocks.note: surface reading: an elderly person who has kept a trim waist
setter's reading: an antique timing device whose narrow waist is famous, giving its name to a curvy figure

explanation.walkthrough: Old-timer is a timekeeper, not a pensioner; the pinched middle of this sand timer gives a slim-waisted figure its name.
explanation.definitionFit: This sand timer has two bulbs joined by a narrow neck, an old way of measuring time with no bulge in the middle.

clue.text: A strange character is Ray, sometimes

blocks.note: first meaning: a letter from a foreign alphabet, the Greek third letter
second meaning: a type of high-energy radiation

explanation.walkthrough: Strange character looks like an eccentric person, and Ray like a man's name; one is a Greek letter, the other radiation.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the third letter of the Greek alphabet, and the name of very penetrating electromagnetic radiation from radioactive decay.

clue.text: A kiss to inspire a Dickensian architect

blocks.note: a peck is a quick kiss
to inspire is literally to breathe in

explanation.surface: A kiss that gives a novelist's designer fresh ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspire is used in its literal sense of inhaling.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth Pecksniff is the hypocritical architect and surveyor in Charles Dickens's novel Martin Chuzzlewit.

clue.text: Scotsman with a ***wife and a bird

blocks.note: Mac is a nickname for a Scot, from the surname prefix
taken as written
the abbreviation used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A Scot accompanied by his wife and a pet bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large, brightly coloured long-tailed parrot from Central and South America.

clue.text: A promenade around the isles is out of this world

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun answer: the place that is out of this world

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a parade is a public walk or esplanade
Is. is the abbreviation for islands or isles

explanation.surface: A seafront walk around some islands is heavenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is heaven, the blissful realm beyond earthly life, and in loose use any idyllic place.

clue.text: A survey of Newfoundland

definitions.note: a prepositional phrase for a proper noun, fair because it reads as 'a place of Newfoundland', naming a town there

blocks.note: first meaning: a look
second meaning: a town in that Canadian province, famous for its airport

explanation.walkthrough: A survey of Newfoundland sounds like a map; instead it is a British slang word for a look, and also a town on that island.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a gander is British slang for taking a look, and Gander is a town in the Canadian province with a well-known airport.
